_readme: Realistic sample payload for the Market News screen, for design work only.
Shapes mirror apps/web/src/api/types.ts exactly (NewsItem / CalendarEvent / TruthPost).
All timestamps are ms epoch and are anchored to `now` below so the mock renders
deterministically ('12m ago' is always '12m ago'). Change `now` and everything shifts.
The Truth Social entries are LABELLED PLACEHOLDER TEXT sized to a typical post —
they are not real posts and must never be presented as such.

headlines.title: Powell says the committee is ‘not on a preset course’ as June PCE cools to 2.4%
headlines.tradeNote: A softer PCE print with no forward commitment keeps the September cut live without pricing it fully. Dollar-negative at the margin — watch EUR/USD hold above the 1.0940 shelf into the 2:00 PM decision, and expect gold to stay bid while real yields drift.

headlines.title: Dollar slips to a three-week low as traders lift September cut odds to 78%
headlines.tradeNote: Rate-cut repricing is doing the work here, not risk appetite. Short-dollar setups across the majors have the wind behind them, but the FOMC statement at 2:00 PM is the binary — size accordingly and be flat or hedged into it.

headlines.title: Gold pushes through $3,480 as real yields slide
headlines.tradeNote: Clean continuation on the metal — the move is yield-driven rather than headline-driven, which tends to hold better. XAU/USD longs stay valid above 3,455; a hawkish hold this afternoon is the obvious invalidation.

headlines.title: Bitcoin holds $118K after $412M of spot ETF inflows
headlines.tradeNote: Flows, not leverage, are carrying this leg — funding is still flat, so the move has room. BTC/USD dips into 116.2K remain buyable while the ETF tape stays positive.

headlines.title: Eurozone flash CPI holds at 2.1%, keeping the ECB on hold into September
headlines.tradeNote: An in-line print removes a euro-side catalyst, so EUR/USD trades off the dollar leg for the rest of the week. Nothing to fade here — it is a non-event that clears the decks for the FOMC.

headlines.title: Nasdaq futures firm as Microsoft and Meta clear the bar after the bell
headlines.tradeNote: Two of the four heaviest weights beat, so the index-level bid is mechanical. US100 longs have support into the open, though a 2:00 PM surprise outranks earnings for the afternoon session.

headlines.title: US and EU agree framework to defer auto tariffs to January
headlines.tradeNote: Removes a tail risk that had been sitting on the euro and on European autos. Modestly EUR-supportive; not a reason to add size on its own.

headlines.title: Fed’s Waller repeats he sees room for two cuts this year
headlines.tradeNote: Waller has said this before, so the marginal information is near zero — the tape barely moved. File it as confirmation of the dovish wing, not a new catalyst.

headlines.title: Oil steadies near $71 as OPEC+ signals no change to October quotas
headlines.tradeNote: Range-bound and off-book for this desk. Only matters second-hand, through the CAD leg and the headline-inflation read.

headlines.title: Ethereum ETF options approved, opening a new hedging venue
headlines.tradeNote: Structural rather than directional — it deepens the market without giving a trade today.

headlines.title: Dow lags as industrials give back Tuesday’s gains
headlines.tradeNote: Rotation inside the index, not a market-wide risk-off. US30 relative weakness against US100 is the only readable signal.

headlines.title: Treasury 10-year yield eases to 4.02% ahead of Friday’s payrolls
headlines.tradeNote: The 4.00% line is the level that matters — a break under it has been reliably gold-positive and dollar-negative all quarter.

headlines.title: Silver tops $41 for the first time since 2011
headlines.tradeNote: Confirms the precious-metals bid rather than adding to it. Not an instrument this desk trades directly.

headlines.title: Japan’s industrial output rebounds 1.8% m/m in June
headlines.body: Factory output rose for a second month, led by autos and semiconductor equipment, the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry said. The reading beat the 1.1% consensus and follows a downwardly revised 0.4% gain in May.

calendar._note: The two entries below are older than 6h, so they land in the dimmed 'Past' block.
calendar.title: German Ifo Business Climate
Advance Goods Trade Balance
calendar.explainer: The first read on the month's goods deficit. It feeds straight into the GDP estimate, so a big miss moves growth forecasts more than it moves the dollar.

calendar.title: FOMC Rate Decision
calendar.explainer: The Fed sets the overnight rate every six weeks. The rate itself is usually priced in — the market trades the statement's wording and any change to the dot plot, so the first ten minutes are the volatile ones.

calendar.title: FOMC Press Conference
calendar.explainer: Powell takes questions thirty minutes after the statement. It routinely produces a bigger move than the decision itself, because this is where the forward guidance gets softened or hardened live.

calendar.title: Eurozone Flash CPI y/y
calendar.explainer: The euro area's first inflation estimate for the month. It is the single number the ECB's next move hangs on, so it moves EUR/USD more than any other European release.

calendar.title: Core PCE Price Index m/m
calendar.explainer: The Fed's preferred inflation gauge, stripped of food and energy. A tenth either side of forecast is enough to reprice the next cut.
